text:
Washington might be the most perfectly average team in the East. The Capitals are 8-6 with 49 goals for and 48 against, on 49.1 expected for and 48.1 against. Their chances say 15.4 points; they have 16. Our simulations project 93 points and a 55% playoff chance, a coin flip with a slight lean.

What makes them interesting is who is carrying it. Jordan Kyrou has 13 points in his last 10 games against 7.2 expected, playing on the one line Tom Gulitti of NHL.com reported stayed intact through a shuffle: Alex Tuch, Dylan Strome and Kyrou. Meanwhile Tom Wilson has no points in his last 10 against 6.1 expected, which reads as a slump in finishing, not a collapse in chances. A line of Wilson, Pierre-Luc Dubois and Aliaksei Protas has won 64% of the expected goals together. Boone Jenner, Justin Sourdif and Ryan Leonard won 74% in limited time and haven't been scored on.

The concerns are in the details. Washington takes 4.29 penalties a game and draws 3.5, and the power play generates only 0.5 expected goals a game. A team this even can't keep giving away the special teams battle.

Our hunch: Wilson's drought ends soon, because the chances are there. When it does, the Capitals will look like more than a .500 team.
headline: Even on paper, uneven on the ice
